neighbours.label: animal sensing and navigation nouns (sense of smell, pheromone trail, swimming direction)
fire: Dogs have a remarkable sense of smell and track scents for miles.
Ants follow a chemical trail left by the first scout.
Salmon use their sense of smell to find the river of their birth.
The larvae change their swimming depth as the light fades.
Bees mark flowers with a scent trail for the rest of the hive.
Sharks can detect blood in the water from a great distance.
Migrating birds keep their direction using the magnetic field.
Moths follow the scent of a mate across the dark meadow.
quiet: Dogs have a remarkable loyalty and stay with families for years.
Ants build large nests under stones in the garden.
Salmon are a popular fish in markets along the coast.
The larvae grow quickly as the water warms in spring.
Bees store honey in wax combs for the rest of the hive.
Sharks have several rows of teeth in their wide jaws.
Migrating birds rest on the lake before the long winter.
Moths are often brown or grey with dusty wings.

notes: Card: ' smell', ' smelling', ' swimming', ' direction', ' trail', ' paths' in animal behaviour text; also code fragments (term).
